key_insight: A2M shows that MCP agents can be hijacked by first attracting tool selection through adversarial metadata and then manipulating outcomes using execution-trace-guided tool returns.
engineering_relevance: For agentic systems that consume third-party tools, the study highlights the need for stricter tool vetting, runtime isolation, and defenses against semantic supply-chain attacks.
method: Optimize attacker-controlled tool metadata to maximize invocation likelihood.
Use execution traces to iteratively refine malicious tool outputs.
Run the framework in a black-box setting across multiple MCP scenarios and transfer it to other models.
evidence_signal: On LiveMCPBench, the method reached 93.6% malicious tool invocation, 32.4× benign token cost under Cognitive Denial of Service, and 74.4% mean attack success across three attack types.
watch_item: The results are strongest on the evaluated MCP benchmark and may depend on how well attack objectives transfer to different agent policies, tools, and runtime defenses.
paper_title: A2M: Trace-Optimized Agent Hijacking in the MCP Ecosystem
